resources.string: Build an installation plan in Devices, then start it in Tasks.
Device history could not be read or saved. Flashing is blocked; keep the app data for diagnosis.
Connect FM-1 instruments through an OTG hub. Identify each instrument, choose its package and review the installation plan. A powered hub is recommended.
Current USB address: %1$s (not a physical hub socket)
No USB serial available. Reconnection requires session continuity and explicit pairing in a multi-device setup.
USB serial observed locally. Cross-mode uniqueness has not been hardware-verified; it does not enable automatic pairing.
Memory type is supplied by you for this attachment. ROM detection is separate and is never assigned automatically.
Names are saved, connections are not. After a lost connection, read and physically identify the instrument before assigning its saved name. Remove its pending job first.
Choose the instrument you physically identified
One instrument at a time. Each task keeps its own target and verified package.
Only one new candidate is allowed and all other instruments must stay connected. Confirm only if this is the instrument being updated. Do not unplug instruments during a write.
Waiting for one unambiguous MIDI connection…
Choose firmware on the device cards to build your plan.
Check the instrument names and package versions above. Keep USB and power connected until verification finishes. Firmware may change instrument settings. Starting here approves this exact plan.
The current write and verification will finish. Remaining tasks stay in the plan.
Result unconfirmed · queue paused; inspect the instrument before a new attempt
The plan no longer matches the current connections or packages. Remove affected tasks, identify the instruments again and rebuild the plan.
This instrument already has a pending task. Remove the task before changing its configuration.
This package is pinned to a task. Remove the pending task before deleting or replacing the package.
Another instrument disconnected. The hub session is no longer trustworthy; no further write will start. Check the devices and rebuild the plan.
The returning USB serial contradicts the selected instrument. Operation stopped.
This USB device exposes multiple MIDI port pairs. Writing is blocked until the correct pair can be identified.
Read your FM-1 over MIDI or use USB download mode to detect its flash chip.
Switch a connected FM-1 from MIDI to USB download mode. This disconnects MIDI.
The app keeps a local operation and error log (daily files, seven days by default; up to 256 KiB per day and 10 MiB total). Export it when reporting a problem. No log is uploaded automatically.
Delete the local operation log? Previously exported files remain unchanged.
Delete all %1$d downloaded firmware packages? You will need to download them again for offline installation. Favorites, device names, history and recovery backups are kept.
Enter a password, token or API key.
Unable to access the encrypted authentication store.
Enter an HTTPS GitHub repository URL: https://github.com/owner/repository.
Confirm compatibility with the publisher. A filename or product version does not identify supported flash chips. Unknown compatibility requires a separate force warning and confirmation.

Secrets are encrypted with Android Keystore and excluded from logs. Leave the secret empty to keep a saved value for the unchanged source and authentication configuration. Entered secrets are cleared on screen recreation.
Authentication required. Enter credentials or authorize this source with OAuth 2.0.
Client secret (optional for public PKCE clients)

For browser sign-in, register redirect URI pl.ekim.fm1-flasher://oauth/callback with your OAuth server. Save the source, then choose Authorize OAuth 2.0. Client Credentials needs a client secret; public PKCE does not.
OAuth 2.0 authorized. You can check this source now.
Complete OAuth 2.0 sign-in in your browser.
OAuth token exchange failed. Check the client, endpoint and granted permissions.
OAuth response is invalid, expired or cancelled. Start authorization again.
Confirm compatibility for each asset with its publisher. Changes are applied after you return to the source form and save. Unknown compatibility requires a separate force warning and confirmation.
Save and check the source first to discover its packages, then configure compatibility for each SHA-256. A different binary requires its own declaration.
